prior_block:
PRICE PRIORS for recurring line types (statistical model fitted on the thresholds t revealed
in earlier games; gross amounts). How to use them:
- The amounts are final thresholds as they were revealed: they already contain whatever
  deductible, VAT and customary-price judgement applied in those cases, and they were computed
  from the full invoiced quantity (the whole quantity was indemnified there). For an
  indemnified line of this type take the stated amount for the line as t as it stands and give
  a price_log_sd that matches the stated range. Do not deduct a deductible from it and do not
  cut the invoiced quantity.
- Deviate only for something this case has and those cases did not: an aggregate cap or
  sub-limit that the lines of this invoice must share, a percentage reduction for a breached
  duty, or a purchase price or sum insured stated in the claim that limits the line.
- Whether a line is indemnified in THIS case is decided by the policy and the claim, not by
  the history. The history only says how often this line type was paid at all. A line type
  that was never indemnified before is usually an ancillary charge the policies do not carry;
  treat it as indemnified only if this policy clearly says so.
- line 3 "Shipping": NOT indemnified (t = 0) in all 5 earlier cases; no price evidence

items.rationale: The bicycle is scheduled at an agreed value of EUR 3,500 under a Bicycle Endorsement, overriding the standard EUR 500 sub-limit for mobility equipment. The frame was damaged in the theft event and is an affected item (2.3.1(b), 7.1.1(b)). Indemnity is capped at the agreed value, but repair/replacement is covered up to the necessary cost, not exceeding that value.

Brakes are a permanently fitted part of the scheduled bicycle and were damaged in the theft event (2.3.1(b), 7.1.1(b)). Covered as part of the repair to the affected item, within the agreed value cap.

Shipping lines have never been indemnified in any reference case and are not listed as a covered cost in Part 5 or 7.1.7. Ancillary charges not required by the repair or recovery are excluded (7.1.8(d), 3.1.5).

Vehicle costs are indemnified only when required for covered repair or recovery work (7.1.7(g), 5.2.2). Here, the service visit was necessary for the repair of the affected bicycle. Reference cases show t per pc about 77 (range 65–88).
Assembly costs are indemnified when required for the repair of an affected item (7.1.7(c)). Reference case t per pc about 109 (range 80–166).
Miscellaneous items lines have never been indemnified in any reference case and are not specifically covered by the policy (7.1.8(d)).
Labour hours are indemnified when required for the repair of an affected item (7.1.7(d)). Reference case t per hr about 36 (range 28–55).
Skilled worker hours have not been indemnified in any reference case for this type of claim; likely considered ancillary or not separately necessary (7.1.8(a)).

Vehicle costs are indemnified when required for recovery of an affected item (5.2.2(a), 7.1.7(g)). Here, the locksmith's attendance was necessary to recover the stolen bicycle. Reference case t per pc about 77 (range 65–88).

Assembly costs are indemnified when required for the recovery of an affected item (5.2.2(b), 7.1.7(c)). The locksmith's work to cut the lock was necessary to recover the bicycle. Reference case t per pc about 109 (range 80–166).
Miscellaneous items lines have never been indemnified in any reference case and are not specifically covered by the policy (7.1.8(d)).
Labour hours are indemnified when required for the recovery of an affected item (5.2.2(b), 7.1.7(d)). Reference case t per hr about 36 (range 28–55).
Skilled worker hours have not been indemnified in any reference case for this type of claim; likely considered ancillary or not separately necessary (7.1.8(a)).
